question: What is the primary mode of transmitting blood-borne viruses through unsafe injections?

options.A: Consuming contaminated water and local foods
options.B: Sharing contaminated needles and unsterile syringes
options.C: Direct skin contact with intact patient epidermis
options.D: Inhaling airborne droplets from infected patients

explanation: Unsterile injection equipment directly introduces infected blood into the recipient's circulatory system. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is Hepatitis B a major risk when using unsterile injection equipment?

options.A: It spreads faster than bacterial infections
options.B: It cannot be prevented by any vaccine
options.C: It survives on surfaces and equipment for a long time
options.D: It destroys white blood cells within minutes

explanation: HBV can live on surfaces and medical equipment longer than many other viruses, making equipment sterilization crucial. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the medical term for a localized collection of pus caused by an unsterile injection?
explanation: Bacteria entering through an unsafe injection can cause a localized infection that traps pus inside the tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h2)

question: A patient returns with spreading redness, warmth, and severe pain at a past injection site. What is this condition called?
explanation: Spreading warmth, pain, and redness in the skin layers are classic signs of a bacterial skin infection known as cellulitis. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h2)

question: Giving an intramuscular injection incorrectly in the buttocks can damage which major nerve?
explanation: The sciatic nerve runs deep through the gluteal region and can be injured if an injection is poorly placed. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h3)

question: What usually causes tissue death (necrosis) after an injection?

options.A: Using a needle that is too small for thick medication
options.B: Irritating medication leaking into surrounding skin or fat
options.C: Not pressing the site long enough after the injection
options.D: Failing to clean the skin before the injection

explanation: Certain drugs damage surrounding cells and cause tissue death when they leak outside of the deep muscle layer. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which vital sign change is an early sign of a systemic infection from a bad injection site?
explanation: Fever is one of the earliest signs that the body is fighting off a spreading bacterial infection. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why do nurses gently press (palpate) a healed injection site during a follow-up assessment?

options.A: To check for hidden deep lumps, hardness, or pain
options.B: To help clear out leftover medication
options.C: To check if the patient has developed immunity
options.D: To measure the thickness of the fat layer

explanation: Palpating helps find underlying issues like hard nodules, deep infections, or nerve damage that you cannot see on the surface. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the immediate nursing care for a patient with a draining injection-site abscess?

options.A: Massaging the area hard to push the fluid out
options.B: Applying dry heat without cleaning the wound
options.C: Putting medicated skin cream over the open wound
options.D: Doing sterile dressing changes and proper wound care

explanation: Open wounds require sterile technique, clean dressing changes, and close monitoring to heal properly. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support important for patients who get a blood-borne infection from unsafe injections?

options.B: Learning about a chronic viral illness causes deep emotional distress
options.C: Counseling replaces the need for drugs
options.D: Talking to patients helps wounds close faster

explanation: Receiving a diagnosis for a lifelong condition like HIV or hepatitis is emotionally heavy and requires supportive counseling. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the safest way to handle a used disposable needle to prevent injury?

options.A: Try to put the cap back on using both hands
options.B: Leave it on a tray until your shift ends
options.C: Drop it straight into a puncture-resistant safety box
options.D: Snap the needle tip off before throwing it away

explanation: Dropping sharps directly into a safety box without recapping is the best way to prevent accidental needle pricks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which action goes against safe injection rules?

options.A: Throwing used sharps into a designated safety container
options.B: Washing hands with soap and water before prepping meds
options.C: Reusing the same syringe for different patients if you change the needle
options.D: Using alcohol swabs to clean rubber vial tops

explanation: Changing only the needle is unsafe; both the syringe and needle are strictly single-use items. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h6)
